comment: Cross-language golden cases for the roster.csv row keep-rule. A roster row is kept when it carries at least ONE identity column — username, github_id, or email — and rejected only when all three are blank. Both the Go strict reader (recordToRow in cli/gh-teacher/internal/configrepo/students_csv.go) and the TS reader (parseRosterCsv in web/src/util/rosterCsv.ts) must agree on every case here, because the web WRITES an email-only pending row when a teacher invites a student by email and the CLI must still read that classroom's roster. `record` lists the canonical columns in header order (username,first_name,last_name,email,section,github_id,role). `keep` is whether the row survives the KEEP-RULE specifically. Two scoping notes, so this fixture is not read as a stronger guarantee than it is: (1) the keep decision is shared, but the two readers act differently on a row they don't keep — the web drops it silently, while Go's strict reader errors (aborting the file) and its lenient reader preserves it verbatim for round-tripping; (2) cases here carry only github_id values the id parser accepts, because Go additionally hard-errors on an unparseable github_id (e.g. `nope`) for ANY row, with or without other identity columns — a pre-existing divergence from the web, which keeps such a row. Update both readers in lockstep.

cases.why: username only — the classic CLI-authored row
email only — the web's pending email-invite row
github_id only — identity without a resolved login
unusable but present github_id still counts as identity
email only, surrounded by whitespace (trimmed before the check)
metadata but no identity column — addresses nobody
whitespace-only cells are blank after trimming
